product_type: Rear combination lamp: exterior lighting and signalling module with rear position, stop and reversing functions and an integrated retro-reflector in a single housing
summary: A rear lamp assembly for an M1 passenger car. It combines a rear position lamp, a stop lamp, a reversing lamp and a passive retro-reflector behind a red outer lens in one housing. The light source is LED modules on a PCB. The exploded-view drawing shows these parts: outer lens, retro-reflector, seal/gasket, a reflector with multiple optical sections, an LED PCB, the housing and fasteners. Drawing callouts state these targets: rear position lamp 4–17 cd on axis, stop lamp 60–185 cd on axis, reversing lamp visible to 45° outboard, red chromaticity, retro-reflector reflectivity at 5° incidence, no water ingress after the spray test, and aim retained under vibration. Materials are representative values only and must be confirmed against the actual bill of materials. Key open points affecting applicability are: whether the reversing section has a white/colourless lens area, the stop lamp category (single or variable intensity), the retro-reflector class, the LED drive electronics (EMC), any other functions (direction indicator, rear fog lamp), and the mounting location (fixed body vs movable component).

questions.question: Does the reversing lamp have its own white/colourless lens zone (e.g. the separate rectangular window seen in the outer lens drawing), or does all light pass through the red lens?
questions.why_it_matters: A reversing lamp must emit white light; a red-only lens would make the reversing function non-compliant, and the answer drives the colorimetric requirements for each zone.

questions.question: Is the stop lamp single-level (constant intensity) or variable intensity, and does any function use a day/night or sequential/variable control?
questions.why_it_matters: It determines the photometric category of the stop and position lamps (fixed vs variable intensity), which have different intensity limits and test requirements.

questions.question: Are the LED light sources non-replaceable, replaceable LED light sources, or a replaceable light source module?
questions.why_it_matters: Replaceable LED light sources must be approved under the light source regulation; non-replaceable LEDs and modules have different marking and test requirements.

questions.question: Does the PCB carry electronic driver/control circuitry (current regulators, microcontroller, failure detection)?
questions.why_it_matters: Electronic sub-assemblies trigger EMC approval requirements and may affect failure-mode and tell-tale requirements.

questions.question: Does the assembly include any additional functions such as a rear direction indicator, rear fog lamp or rear side marker?
questions.why_it_matters: Each additional function brings its own photometric, colour and installation requirements, and may change the grouping/combination assessment.

questions.question: Where is the lamp mounted: fixed body panel, tailgate/boot lid, or split across both?
questions.why_it_matters: Mounting on movable components triggers specific installation provisions and may require an interdependent lamp system or additional lamps.

questions.question: Is the retro-reflector intended as a rear red non-triangular retro-reflector (Class IA/IB) and is it the vehicle's mandatory rear retro-reflector?
questions.why_it_matters: It sets the retro-reflector class, colour, CIL values and installation requirements, and determines whether a separate retro-reflector is needed.

questions.question: Is the lamp intended for use on vehicle categories other than M1 (e.g. N1 derivatives)?
questions.why_it_matters: The installation regulations differ by vehicle category, and broader category use would extend the scope of compliance verification.
